stem: The root system has expanded substantially and containers now reach the same dryback threshold much earlier each day. What change is best supported?
choices: Keep irrigation timing unchanged because container volume still provides the same total water-storage capacity
Increase nutrient concentration so each event supplies more fertilizer as root mass and canopy demand increase
Reassess irrigation timing or frequency against faster measured depletion while preserving root-zone aeration
Delay irrigation until mild wilting develops so the expanded root system receives a stronger dryback signal
rationale: As root systems and transpiring canopies develop, water use can increase. Irrigation timing should respond to measured depletion while preserving an appropriate air-water balance.
